A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, references, appendices, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation comparisons, label-error analyses, ensemble experiments, and fine-tuning results on four TRUE datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds LLM annotations and analyses of SummEval, alongside new model-specific analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adapts the ensemble procedure to five-level ordinal predictions, requiring a rating difference greater than one before confidence-based flagging (Section 3; Appendix A.2). The underlying probability averaging and binary filtering/flipping procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The four TRUE datasets are retained, and SummEval adds CNN/DailyMail summaries evaluated for coherence, relevance, consistency, and fluency. Its ordinal ratings substantially extend coverage beyond the earlier binary factual-consistency setting.

E2.justification: The added SummEval agreement comparison individually evaluates GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Flash as annotator groups (Table 5), extending the model comparisons beyond those in the corresponding TRUE analysis. The existing TRUE comparator sets, nine-model performance comparison, and training controls remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new SummEval protocol uses median-aggregated crowd and expert ratings, relative distance to expert labels, Pearson correlation, and ordinal Krippendorff’s alpha. Appendix E also introduces model-specific confidence bins. These are substantial additions to evaluation design; the existing TRUE sampling and fine-tuning settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds separate confidence/error-detection analyses for four LLMs (Appendix E, Figure 13) and examines fine-tuned models’ class predictions on corrected versus unchanged examples (Appendix F.2). It also extends confidence and ensemble-size analyses to SummEval. Earlier filtering/flipping and validation-set ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five fine-tuning seeds, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals using 100 resamples, and Clopper–Pearson intervals with finite-population correction. Additional plots extend the existing reporting practices without establishing a changed uncertainty procedure or increased run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds SummEval results, including expert–LLM correlation of 0.57 versus expert–crowd correlation of 0.04 (Figure 7), agreement statistics (Table 5), and confidence/ensemble curves. Model-specific findings and class-prediction frequencies are also new. Corresponding TRUE Tables 2–4 and training-result plots retain their earlier values.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces a precise ordinal-disagreement definition requiring a score gap greater than one, extending the earlier binary disagreement relation. This is a limited mathematical-definition addition; no theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: confident ensemble disagreements identify label errors, LLM annotations compare favorably with human annotations, and correcting labels affects training and evaluation performance. The headline improvements of up to 4% and 15% are retained. SummEval supplies additional support without materially changing these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning crowd-worker qualifications, contamination, prompting, aggregation, and task coverage. It explicitly frames SummEval as a simulated crowd-label setting, discusses legitimate annotation variation, and adds interpretations of individual-model calibration and fine-tuned models’ learned label bias.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the GPT-4 snapshot and documents SummEval model versions, JSON outputs, and probability extraction. Conversely, v1’s Table 7 containing full dataset sizes is removed. Existing binary prompts, annotation instructions, hardware, and fine-tuning hyperparameters remain available.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against annotation-error detection research, distinguishing its zero-shot confident-disagreement approach from trained detectors. It adds works including Klie, Weber-Genzel, Yang, and Bavaresco. The earlier dedicated factual-consistency survey and references such as QAFactEval and WeCheck are removed.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively reorganized: related work moves forward and incorporates annotation background, the method receives a separate rewritten section, and detailed dataset descriptions and annotation comparisons move to appendices. v2 also adds an appendix contents list and a dedicated limitations section.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figures 2, 3, and 7 combine TRUE and SummEval panels; Figure 13 and Table 5 add new displays. Existing displays are relocated or relabeled, and the earlier dataset-size Table 7 is removed.

improvement.justification: SummEval substantially strengthens validation beyond v1’s binary setting by evaluating ordinal, multidimensional annotations against independently supplied expert ratings. The new model-specific and label-bias analyses improve support for the ensemble rationale and interpretation of fine-tuned-model behavior. Explicit qualifications also sharpen the crowdsourcing conclusions. SummEval remains a simulated crowd-label setting, and some dataset-size documentation is lost, but the gains in validation and interpretation are substantial.
